items.title: Euler state, flux, positive set and numerical roles
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Fix a constant $\gamma>1$. The one-dimensional ideal-gas Euler state is
$U=(\rho,m,E)\in\mathcal G_\gamma\subset\mathbb R^3$, where
$$\mathcal G_\gamma=\left\{(\rho,m,E):\rho>0,\quad E-\frac{m^2}{2\rho}>0\right\}.$$
For $U\in\mathcal G_\gamma$, define the pressure, velocity, sound speed, and
flux by
$$p(U)=(\gamma-1)\left(E-\frac{m^2}{2\rho}\right),\qquad u(U)=\frac m\rho,\qquad c(U)=\sqrt{\frac{\gamma p(U)}{\rho}},\qquad F(U)=\left(m,\frac{m^2}{\rho}+p(U),u(U)(E+p(U))\right).$$
Thus $\mathcal G_\gamma$ is exactly the set with positive density and positive
pressure; every displayed map is defined on that open set.

For a periodic uniform mesh with $N\ge2$ cells, width $\Delta x>0$, and time
step $\Delta t\ge0$, index cells by $i\in\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z$ and put
$\lambda=\Delta t/\Delta x$. Given cell states $U_i\in\mathcal G_\gamma$, a
shared-face flux is one vector $\widehat F_{i+1/2}\in\mathbb R^3$ assigned to
each face and used in both adjacent cell balances. When produced by a
two-state numerical flux $\widehat F(U_L,U_R)$, it is consistent if
$\widehat F(U,U)=F(U)$ for every $U\in\mathcal G_\gamma$. The associated
one-step update in conservative finite-volume form is
$$U_i^+=U_i-\lambda\left(\widehat F_{i+1/2}-\widehat F_{i-1/2}\right).$$
This shared-face form means that the same face vector appears with opposite
signs in the two neighboring cell updates. A step is admissible when every
output state $U_i^+$ belongs to $\mathcal G_\gamma$; this is a property to
prove under specific flux and time-step hypotheses, not part of the update
definition.

When the HLL middle branch is used at a face, its supplied speeds satisfy
$S_L<0<S_R$ and the flux is
$$\widehat F_{\rm HLL}(U_L,U_R)=\frac{S_RF(U_L)-S_LF(U_R)+S_LS_R(U_R-U_L)}{S_R-S_L}.$$
The speeds are supplied data; their appearance in this formula does not assert
that they enclose the waves of an exact nonlinear Riemann solution. The
ratio $\lambda$ is the time step divided by cell width and is not a physical
viscosity.

For a specified convex entropy pair, write $v$ for its entropy variable and
$F^{ec}$ for a consistent entropy-conservative two-point flux. If $D$ is a
symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix, meaning $z^TDz\ge0$ for every vector
$z$, and $F^{ec}$ satisfies
$$\bigl(v(U_R)-v(U_L)\bigr)^T F^{ec}(U_L,U_R)=\psi(U_R)-\psi(U_L),$$
where $\psi$ is the corresponding entropy potential, the entropy-stable
dissipative flux is
$$F^{es}(U_L,U_R)=F^{ec}(U_L,U_R)-\frac12D(U_L,U_R)\bigl(v(U_R)-v(U_L)\bigr).$$
Here $v=\nabla\eta$ for the chosen entropy $\eta$, and the entropy-conservative
flux satisfies the corresponding entropy-variable jump identity. This is a
separate flux condition; it includes no fully discrete time-step entropy
inequality. Conservation, admissibility, entropy stability, and convergence
therefore name different properties and require their own hypotheses.

The following schematic view shows the orientation of one shared face flux.
Positive flux points to the right; the same vector leaves cell $i$ and enters
cell $i+1$. The diagram records the indexing convention only; the update
formula supplies the definition used in proofs.

~~~tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[x=1.15cm,y=1cm]
  \draw (0,0) rectangle (2,0.7);
  \draw (2,0) rectangle (4,0.7);
  \draw (4,0) rectangle (6,0.7);
  \node at (1,0.35) {$U_{i-1}$};
  \node at (3,0.35) {$U_i$};
  \node at (5,0.35) {$U_{i+1}$};
  \draw[->] (1.55,1.1) -- (2.45,1.1);
  \draw[->] (3.55,1.1) -- (4.45,1.1);
  \node at (2,1.4) {$\widehat F_{i-1/2}$};
  \node at (4,1.4) {$\widehat F_{i+1/2}$};
\end{tikzpicture}
~~~

items.title: Ideal-gas LLF admissibility specialization
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Fix $\gamma>1$, an integer $N\ge2$, a width $\Delta x>0$, a time step
$\Delta t\ge0$, and a periodic array of one-dimensional ideal-gas Euler states
$U_i=(\rho_i,m_i,E_i)\in\mathcal G_\gamma\subset\mathbb R^3$, indexed by
$i\in\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z$. For each state set
$$p_i=(\gamma-1)\left(E_i-\frac{m_i^2}{2\rho_i}\right),\qquad u_i=\frac{m_i}{\rho_i},\qquad c_i=\sqrt{\frac{\gamma p_i}{\rho_i}},\qquad F_i=\left(m_i,\frac{m_i^2}{\rho_i}+p_i,u_i(E_i+p_i)\right),$$
where
$$\mathcal G_\gamma=\left\{(\rho,m,E):\rho>0,\quad E-\frac{m^2}{2\rho}>0\right\}.$$
At every face choose a supplied speed $a_{i+1/2}$ satisfying
$$a_{i+1/2}\ge\max\bigl(|u_i|+c_i,\ |u_{i+1}|+c_{i+1}\bigr),\qquad 2\lambda a_{i+1/2}\le1,\qquad \lambda=\frac{\Delta t}{\Delta x}.$$
Use the symmetric HLL speeds $S_L=-a_{i+1/2}$ and $S_R=a_{i+1/2}$, so that
$$\widehat F_{i+1/2}=\frac12(F_i+F_{i+1})-\frac{a_{i+1/2}}2(U_{i+1}-U_i),\qquad U_i^+=U_i-\lambda\left(\widehat F_{i+1/2}-\widehat F_{i-1/2}\right).$$
Then $U_i^+\in\mathcal G_\gamma$ for every cell $i$; in particular, each
updated density and pressure is strictly positive. This conclusion is for the
specified one-step symmetric branch and does not assert positivity for other
HLL speed pairs or a fully discrete entropy inequality.

items.title: Shared-face flux telescoping conservation
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Fix $\gamma>1$, an integer $N\ge2$, a cell width $\Delta x>0$, a time step
$\Delta t\ge0$, and periodic cell states $U_i=(\rho_i,m_i,E_i)\in\mathcal G_\gamma$
for $i\in\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z$. Assign one vector flux
$\widehat F_{i+1/2}\in\mathbb R^3$ to each periodic face and use that same
value in both neighboring cell updates
$$U_i^+=U_i-\lambda\left(\widehat F_{i+1/2}-\widehat F_{i-1/2}\right),\qquad \lambda=\frac{\Delta t}{\Delta x}.$$
Define the total conserved vector before and after the step by
$$M=\Delta x\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z}U_i,\qquad M^+=\Delta x\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z}U_i^+.$$
Then $M^+=M$. Thus the total density, momentum, and total energy components
are unchanged by this periodic shared-face update. This algebraic conservation
claim alone does not assert admissibility, entropy stability, or convergence.

items.title: Entropy, invariant-domain and weak-limit hypotheses
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
The relevant numerical properties have separate hypotheses. A shared-face
finite-volume update on a periodic uniform grid with $N\ge2$ cells of common
width $\Delta x>0$ uses the same ratio $\lambda=\Delta t/\Delta x$ in every
cell, where $\Delta t\ge0$. Its balance is
$$U_i^+=U_i-\lambda(\widehat F_{i+1/2}-\widehat F_{i-1/2}),\qquad i\in\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z,$$
with one vector flux per face shared by the two neighboring cells. Finite
telescoping conserves $\sum_iU_i$, and hence the total vector
$\Delta x\sum_iU_i$. That algebra alone gives no membership of the updated states
in an admissible set, entropy inequality, or convergence result.

For the symmetric ideal-gas HLL/LLF branch, the stated one-step positivity
result assumes $a\ge\max(|u_L|+c_L,|u_R|+c_R)$ and $2\lambda a\le1$ at every
face. For a general HLL middle branch, the convex invariant-domain result uses a
different explicit hypothesis. Let $K$ be a convex state set, meaning every
segment joining two members lies in $K$, and write $\nu=\Delta t/h$ for the
time-step-to-cell-width ratio in this HLL formula. The approximate HLL fan at a
face with $S_L<0<S_R$ has middle state
$$U_*=\frac{S_RU_R-S_LU_L-(F_R-F_L)}{S_R-S_L}.$$
This is the state in the two-wave approximation; its associated model flux is
not assumed to be the physical flux $F(U_*)$. The fan is $U_L$ to the left of
$S_L$, $U_*$ between $S_L$ and $S_R$, and $U_R$ to the right of $S_R$. Its
spatial averages over the left and right adjacent half-cells at time
$\Delta t$, respectively, are
$$A^-=(1-2\nu(-S_L))U_L+2\nu(-S_L)U_*,\qquad A^+=(1-2\nu S_R)U_R+2\nu S_RU_*,$$
under the one-sided bounds $2\nu(-S_L)\le1$ and $2\nu S_R\le1$. The HLL
invariant-domain result assumes both half-cell averages lie in $K$ at every
face and every cell mean lies in $K$. Since each cell update is the average of
its two adjacent half-cell averages, convexity then gives the updated mean in
$K$. A sufficient way to verify the fan-average hypothesis is to show
$U_L,U_R,U_*\in K$; the result does not infer $U_*\in K$ from supplied endpoint
speed estimates alone.

The sketch fixes the fan and half-cell conventions used in those formulas.
The horizontal axis is $x$, with $x=0$ at the face. The vertical arrow at the
left marks increasing time $t$ and is offset for readability; the label $0$
marks the face at $t=0$. The wave lines have supplied speeds $S_L<0<S_R$, with
their slopes representing $dx/dt$. The dashed verticals mark the adjacent cell
centers at $-h/2$ and $h/2$. The one-sided CFL bounds keep each wave inside its
half-cell through time $\Delta t$. The proof and averages are the displayed
algebraic formulas, not the drawing.

~~~tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[x=2cm,y=1.15cm]
  \draw[->] (-1.35,0) -- (1.45,0) node[right] {$x$};
  \draw[->] (-1.3,0) -- (-1.3,1.2) node[above] {$t$};
  \draw[dashed] (-0.5,0) -- (-0.5,1.05);
  \draw[dashed] (0.5,0) -- (0.5,1.05);
  \draw[thick] (0,0) -- (-0.34,1);
  \draw[thick] (0,0) -- (0.34,1);
  \node at (-0.95,0.7) {$U_L$};
  \node at (0,0.68) {$U_*$};
  \node at (0.95,0.7) {$U_R$};
  \node[below] at (-0.5,0) {$-h/2$};
  \node[below] at (0.5,0) {$h/2$};
  \node[above right] at (-0.34,1) {$S_L$};
  \node[above left] at (0.34,1) {$S_R$};
  \node[below right] at (0,0) {$0$};
  \node[left] at (-1.3,1) {$\Delta t$};
\end{tikzpicture}
~~~

The entropy-stable dissipative-flux definition specifies a consistent
entropy-conservative flux with positive-semidefinite entropy-variable
dissipation, and explicitly supplies no fully discrete time-step inequality.
Any semidiscrete entropy inequality for a selected semidiscrete evolution is a
separate result; a fully discrete bound also requires an argument for the
chosen time integrator. The ratio $\nu$ above is only the mesh time-step to
width ratio and is not physical viscosity.

For the convex-scaling limiter, assume additionally that $K\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
is closed, meaning it contains every limit in $\mathbb R^m$ of a convergent
sequence of its members; $K$ remains convex. The limiter applies to a finite nonempty set of node states
$V_j\in\mathbb R^m$ with positive weights $w_j$ summing to one and an already
admissible mean $\bar V=\sum_jw_jV_j\in K$. It returns the largest
$\theta\in[0,1]$ for which all scaled states
$V_j^\theta=\bar V+\theta(V_j-\bar V)$ belong to $K$. The feasible parameter
set is closed in $[0,1]$ and contains $0$, so this maximum exists. Direct summation gives
$$\sum_jw_jV_j^\theta=\sum_jw_j\bar V+\theta\left(\sum_jw_jV_j-\sum_jw_j\bar V\right)=\bar V+\theta(\bar V-\bar V)=\bar V.$$
Thus the construction preserves the supplied mean and constrains the chosen
nodes; it has no admissibility branch for a mean outside $K$ and gives no
pointwise-in-cell assertion between those nodes.

The conservative finite-volume weak-limit theorem is a separate scalar
one-dimensional result on $\mathbb R$. It assumes $T>0$, a continuous scalar
flux $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, initial data
$u_0\in L^\infty(\mathbb R)\cap L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R)$, a continuous
consistent numerical flux $F:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$, initial cell averages,
$h_m,\tau_m\to0$, and the Axiom of Countable Choice
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ (for every family $(X_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ of nonempty sets,
there is a function $f:\mathbb N\to\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}X_n$ with
$f(n)\in X_n$ for every $n$). Strong local $L^1$ convergence of the reconstructed states and
local uniform bounds on every bounded space-time cylinder through $t=0$ are
also hypotheses. Under them the limit is a locally bounded scalar
distributional weak solution. In its proof, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used only
in the local spatial-translation step of the face-flux convergence lemma; the
discrete summation and limit passage require no further choice. The theorem
assumes neither a CFL condition nor
an entropy inequality, proves neither convergence nor compactness, and does
not apply to the compressible Euler system.

title: Compressible numerical conservation and admissibility — Examples

items.title: Constant Euler state preserved by consistent shared flux
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Fix $\gamma>1$, $N\ge2$, $\Delta x>0$, and $\Delta t\ge0$ on a periodic uniform
grid. Let
$$\mathcal G_\gamma=\left\{(\rho,m,E)\in\mathbb R^3:\rho>0,\quad E-\frac{m^2}{2\rho}>0\right\}$$
and choose a constant state $U=(\rho,m,E)\in\mathcal G_\gamma$. Its ideal-gas
Euler flux is
$$F(U)=\left(m,\frac{m^2}{\rho}+(\gamma-1)\left(E-\frac{m^2}{2\rho}\right),\frac m\rho\left(E+(\gamma-1)\left(E-\frac{m^2}{2\rho}\right)\right)\right).$$
Set $U_i=U$ in every cell and use one consistent shared face flux at each
interface, meaning $\widehat F_{i+1/2}(U,U)=F(U)$. For the update
$$U_i^+=U_i-\lambda\left(\widehat F_{i+1/2}-\widehat F_{i-1/2}\right),\qquad \lambda=\frac{\Delta t}{\Delta x},$$
every cell remains exactly $U_i^+=U$. This is a one-step constant-state
fixed-point calculation; it does not assert any other stability or convergence
property.
